chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il al-Maythami from Hammad from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who said to his wife: 'If I marry another woman upon you or take a concubine, you are divorced.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is of no effect.' Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever stipulates a condition other than the Book of Allah (Exalted and Mighty), that condition is not valid for him nor upon him.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ ذَلِكَ بِشَيْءٍ: That is of no effect / invalid

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a monogamy clause in a Shia marriage contract?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the validity of monogamy clauses in marriage contracts, clarifying that while the condition is not legally binding (*laysa shay'an*), it reflects the Prophet’s principle that conditions outside the explicit Book of Allah lack enforceability. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between a condition that creates a right versus one that is merely permissible but not obligatory, emphasizing that the husband remains free to exercise his right to polygyny without penalty despite the stipulation.
